name: Trotskyism
summary: Trotskyism is a Marxist current following Leon Trotsky, centred on permanent revolution, working-class self-emancipation through soviets, and proletarian internationalism. It opposes Stalinism and socialism in one country, holding the Soviet bureaucracy a parasitic caste on a degenerated workers' state that needed a political revolution. It seeks a democratically planned, expropriated economy and uses transitional demands to bridge present struggles and revolution.
scope: Mainstream Trotskyism as set out by Trotsky himself in the 1930s (The Transitional Program, The Revolution Betrayed, Their Morals and Ours, writings on the Jewish question) and carried on by the Fourth International tradition. Modern positions on gender, sexuality, climate and migration are inferred and marked low confidence; splinter variants such as Posadism and Third Camp positions are excluded.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Transitional demands aim at decent living conditions for all, which Trotskyists extend to free public health care.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The program demands a guaranteed minimum wage and a sliding scale tied to prices.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Trotskyists favour a democratically planned economy over market allocation.

public-ownership.rationale: The program calls for expropriating key industries and merging banks into one state credit institution.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Adherents demand expropriation of the capitalist class, so far higher taxes on the rich are a minimum.

unions-good.rationale: Revolutionaries work inside mass unions but warn that unions are not ends in themselves and criticise their bureaucrats.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private ownership of the means of production is to be expropriated, not protected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred: they prefer workers' control and expropriation, but would back tighter controls as a step.

cut-welfare.rationale: Transitional demands push for more security for workers, never cuts.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: they favour nationalised industry under workers' control rather than separate worker-owned firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: distrust of the bourgeois state's security apparatus.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from opposition to police interference in private life; not a defining position.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents split between opposing state censorship and fighting racist organisations.

strong-leader.rationale: Trotsky condemned bureaucratic one-man rule under Stalin and favoured soviet democracy.

state-harmful.rationale: Marxists expect the state to wither away eventually but hold a workers' state is needed in the transition.

limit-guns.rationale: The program calls for arming workers in a militia, so they oppose disarming workers.

empower-police-military.rationale: The program calls for replacing the standing army with a people's militia.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Adherents are split; the tradition has no settled position.

decide-locally.rationale: They favour local soviets but within a centrally coordinated plan and international organisation.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred: crime is seen as rooted in class society and punishment as counterproductive.

traditional-family.rationale: Trotsky held the family must be replaced by collective institutions and saw its return as a retreat.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic: modern Trotskyist parties support it, but the founders did not address it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Trotsky condemned the 1936 Soviet abortion ban as police interference in intimate life.

more-religion-public.rationale: Marxist materialists oppose a larger public role for religion, though Trotsky criticised crude anti-religious campaigns.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from the program's denunciation of anti-Semitism and national chauvinism.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: Trotsky stressed social, not natural, causes of women's burdens.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and opposition to national chauvinism.

gradual-change.rationale: The program holds capitalism cannot be reformed and calls for revolutionary conquest of power.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from proletarian internationalism and opposition to chauvinism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: They regard bodies of imperialist governments as tools of capitalist powers while favouring workers' international organisation.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred: they see free trade as a capitalist and imperialist arrangement, but would not back protection for its own sake.

nation-first.rationale: Proletarian internationalism and world revolution are central.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The program opposes imperialist governments and their wars.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from internationalism; modern Trotskyists generally support open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred: they see scarcity as a product of capitalism and favour planned abundance.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic: modern Trotskyists call for planned, anti-capitalist climate action.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Productive forces matter, but social revolution is the precondition.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The founders never addressed it and modern adherents are split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Revolutionary conquest of power by the working class is the central goal.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from opposition to rule by a bureaucratic caste and from workers' self-emancipation.

central-planning.rationale: Trotsky advocated a democratically planned economy, combined in the transition with some market mechanisms.

socialized-markets.rationale: Trotsky accepted markets and money during the transition but not as the lasting basis of socialism.

land-value-tax.rationale: Inferred: a single tax is a reformist substitute for expropriation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the demand to expropriate capitalist wealth.

basic-income.rationale: They prefer guaranteed work and a sliding scale of hours to an unconditional payment.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred: no position beyond a state monopoly of foreign trade for a workers' state.

state-directs-investment.rationale: A planned economy directs investment under democratic control.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The program calls for collective ownership of industry; small farmers are allies, not the model.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred: long-run communist goal, though money is kept during the transition.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The program calls for a single state credit institution, the opposite of market money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: They reject class collaboration and state-run labour-capital bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Trotsky rejected the one-party ban as a permanent principle and argued multiple parties can exist within soviet democracy.

democracy-best.rationale: They defend soviet democracy but treat bourgeois democracy as a historical stage.

direct-votes.rationale: They favour delegate councils; direct referendums are used tactically.

workers-councils.rationale: Council (soviet) power is the core of the political programme.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from support for self-determination of colonial peoples.

natural-rulers.rationale: Opposed to rule by any hereditary or natural elite.

political-violence-never.rationale: Trotsky states there is no bridge to socialism save revolutionary, violent means.

separate-church-state.rationale: Trotsky favoured neutrality of the state on religion and criticised both persecution and accommodation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Trotsky rejected religious morality as class ideology.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Opposed to privatising state functions; they want a workers' militia.

military-superiority.rationale: The program opposes arms races and calls for confiscating war profits.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The program calls national chauvinism and anti-Semitism malignant products of capitalism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Trotsky treats history as the struggle of classes.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Trotsky criticised growing inequality in the USSR, though he accepted unequal pay in the transition.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from support for colonial peoples' liberation.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from support for colonial liberation struggles.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from class internationalism over religious or civilisational blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Trotsky grounded morality in class solidarity.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred: they oppose a bureaucratic state demanding duties of citizens.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not a Trotskyist doctrine; modern ecosocialists vary.

limit-population.rationale: Trotsky wanted the economic causes of abortion removed rather than state limits.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Rapid industrialisation was supported, but not disruption for its own sake.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on democratic workers' control.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from mistrust of state surveillance of workers' organisations.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Trotsky tied means to the class goal, not to ideology-free pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: They combine mass action and strikes with work in unions and, tactically, elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Trotsky said means and ends are dialectically linked and not all means are permissible, but accepted revolutionary violence.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Opposed; they seek abundance through planned industry.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred: the higher stage of communism, which Trotsky said Soviet inequality was far from.

production-for-use.rationale: The planned economy is meant to ensure decent living for all instead of profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxist doctrine adopted by Trotskyism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Trotsky supported the dictatorship of the proletariat, distinguished from bourgeois dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation is the aim but must rest on free consent, not compulsion.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The program calls war the product of capitalism and imperialism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Opposite of their view of taxation and expropriation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Inferred from class-based analysis of rights.

conscription.rationale: They favour a voluntary workers' militia over the standing army, but not on principle.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred: democratic voice via councils is the check.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the demand for material security for all.

media-academia-power.rationale: They hold the capitalist class holds real power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Inferred from the program's attack on racial chauvinism.

organic-representation.rationale: They favour council democracy of workers, not corporate bodies.

total-state.rationale: Trotsky condemned the Stalinist totalitarian bureaucracy.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rejects nationalist rebirth movements and fascism.

universal-morality.rationale: Trotsky explicitly rejects eternal supra-class morality.

single-common-good.rationale: Politics is class struggle between opposed interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Trotsky called Zionism incapable of solving the Jewish question, though he allowed a voluntary Jewish territory under a socialist federation.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inferred from his scepticism of territorial Zionism.

revive-national-language.rationale: Trotsky and his successors took no documented position on national-language revival.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The program demands workers' control and factory committees.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from support for public provision and opposition to privatisation.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not a concern; they hold Keynesian stimulus cannot end the crisis.

economic-freedom.rationale: They reject that capitalism underpins political freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on institutions and class power.

national-self-determination.rationale: The program backs colonial peoples' wars of liberation, while distrusting nationalism.

force-without-un.rationale: They oppose imperialist governments' use of force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Trotsky rejects religious grounds for morality.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the demand for decent living for all.

class-collaboration.rationale: The program rejects Popular Front and class-collaboration politics.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred: Marxists seek to inherit culture, not destroy it.

dominated-front.rationale: They support colonial struggles but not backing local bourgeois governments.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Trotsky wrote of women's legal equality and the need to socialise domestic work.

ban-interest.rationale: They prefer expropriating banks to banning lending.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Trotsky called soviets organs of class rule, and treated states as class instruments.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; modern Trotskyists favour planned transition.

elite-replacement.rationale: Rejects such conspiracy theories as chauvinism.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Trotsky showed women bear the burdens of childbearing and housework, though he stressed class.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Trotsky said the Soviet bureaucracy was a privileged caste and bourgeois politics serves capital.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state interference in reproduction.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from opposition to Stalinist terror.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: They oppose racism and treat racial hostility as a product of capitalist decline.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equal rights are supported though Trotsky rejects abstract universal morality.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Permanent revolution and opposition to socialism in one country are defining Trotskyist positions.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred from Trotsky's anti-imperialism; he saw Zionist settlement in Palestine as a dead end sustained by British imperialism.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred: Trotsky wanted family and personal status freed from religious authority and made equal, as in his critique of the family retreat.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred: Trotsky opposed administrative coercion on religion and favored persuasion and education, so legal limits are rejected.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: a materialist tradition would not legislate religious taboos into law.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The tradition demands separation of school from church and secular public education.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Trotsky defended the USSR against attack but held that a growing bureaucratic state is the problem and the state must wither away.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Inferred: rule by workers' soviets through free participation, though the tradition rests legitimacy on class rule more than consent as such.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxists hold that ruling ideas and morals reflect the ruling class, which Trotsky applies to morality, though he also claims a scientific Marxism; inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trotskyism is internationalist and plans production for need, so national export surpluses are not a goal; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Trotskyism opposes national oppression and rests on proletarian internationalism, so expelling a minority is rejected.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Their Morals and Ours defends revolutionary force when the end is liberation, rejecting the idea that force is wrong whatever the goal.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Class struggle and planned cooperation, not rivalry between individuals or peoples, are the Marxist engine of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Trotsky held party bans under the Soviets to be a wartime measure and called for soviet party freedom, but backed force against fascists; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Wage dependence on capital as unfreedom fits the Marxist critique of wage slavery, though Trotsky does not use this vocabulary; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Trotsky's soviet democracy joins legislative and executive power in workers' councils and rejects bourgeois checks and balances.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Transitional Program states that the crisis of mankind is the crisis of revolutionary leadership and calls for a party to lead the working class.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Transitional Program puts a living wage, jobs and protection against price rises at the head of its demands for the working class and the poorest layers.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Inferred: the program calls for expropriating property under workers' control, not extending private ownership.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The program backs strikes, picket lines and factory occupations as tools of workers' struggle.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxists reject Malthusian explanations; the program blames capitalist relations for unemployment and want.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Proletarian internationalism holds that workers of all peoples share a common interest against capital.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred: Trotsky's model is elected soviets of workers' delegates, not lotteries.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Trotsky defended revolutionary coercion against class enemies as justified by the end, though for the working class and not the state.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The program calls for committees of workers and housewives to control prices and a sliding scale tied to the cost of living.

party-controls-media.rationale: Trotsky condemned the bureaucracy's suppression of criticism and called for freedom for soviet parties, while wanting bourgeois parties barred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred: the program calls for a workers' militia and soldiers' committees, not party command of the army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and the program's call for equal rights for foreign workers.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Trotskyists take the Paris Commune model of officials on a workman's wage as the standard of workers' democracy and attack bureaucratic privilege.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Trotskyist parties follow democratic centralism: free debate, then unity in action once a decision is taken.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred: Trotskyists favour a socialist united states of Europe but regard the capitalist EU as an imperialist bloc to be opposed, not a body to deepen.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Transitional Program wants commanders chosen by workers' organizations and a workers' militia, and the state to be the soviets, not a ruler.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Inferred: Trotsky favoured separation of church and state and secularism, so a state-linked national church governed from above is rejected.

clerical-rule.rationale: Trotsky treated religion as a conservative force and held that power belongs to workers' soviets, so clerical rule is firmly rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The Transitional Program states that the defeat of one's own imperialist government is the lesser evil and the chief enemy is at home.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Trotsky opposed bureaucratic command over art and held that art needs freedom, though he allowed revolutionary defence against counter-revolution.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred: the issue is framed in soviet democracy by revocability of delegates rather than term limits, so no clear position on presidential terms.

recall-officials.rationale: Soviet democracy as Trotskyists describe it rests on delegates revocable at any time, the Commune principle.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Trotskyists oppose imperialist alliances and wars and call for working-class internationalism instead, though they defend workers' states.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Socialisation of housing, not universal private ownership, is the Marxist aim; personal property is kept, inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Transitional Program calls for replacing the standing army with a workers' people's militia.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Marxism treats the urban proletariat as the revolutionary class and criticises rural isolation, inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Trotsky backed self-determination and a united, independent Ukraine; inferred for partitions imposed by powers.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Trotskyists rely on intellectuals and workers alike and distrust bureaucrats, so adherents are split; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Internationalism rejects ranking peoples and Trotsky opposed racism, inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: Modern Trotskyists oppose capital punishment under capitalist states, though Trotsky defended revolutionary terror; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Trotsky criticised the Soviet reversal of women's emancipation and the family, favouring social equality of the sexes.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Marxist materialism and secularism oppose religious teaching in schools; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; Trotskyists oppose state moralising but also exploitation in the industry, inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Proletarian internationalism rejects descent-based belonging and favours open borders, inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Trotsky defended national minorities' cultural rights against oppression, inferred from his writings on the national question.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Trotskyists oppose religious persecution but also special privileges, so adherents split; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Trotsky held that revolution should free everyday life and personality; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from the Transitional Program's anti-imperialist demands; Trotskyists favour repudiating imperialist debts, though this is not a headline demand there.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Permanent revolution holds that backward countries cannot achieve real independence without socialist transformation, and the Transitional Program ties colonial struggles to expropriation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Trotsky backed democratic demands such as a constituent assembly in countries lacking democracy as transitional steps, while preferring soviets once the working class acts; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Trotsky condemned the Soviet bureaucracy for suppressing the political freedom of workers and soviets and held that socialist democracy is needed for planning.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Proletarian internationalism implies duties of wealthy-country workers and states toward the poor, though Trotskyists look to revolution rather than aid; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred: Trotskyists oppose capitalist states' armaments and favour workers' militias, but have supported defence of workers' states.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Trotskyists favour revocable delegates and soviet structures over presidencies, but have used elected-office demands tactically; adherents are split.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The Transitional Program demands expropriation of the banks and a single state bank under workers' control, the opposite of independent central banks.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Trotsky rejected nationalist claims to Palestine as a solution and opposed territorial schemes for Jews under imperialism; inferred for homeland claims generally.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Trotskyists favour expropriating capital and subordinating property to collective planning in the common interest.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Trotsky called the USSR a degenerated workers' state, not capitalist; later state-capitalist readings are the Third Camp split, excluded from this profile.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred: a democratically planned economy would weigh long-term environmental risks that profit-driven firms ignore.

collective-defense.rationale: Trotskyists oppose imperialist alliances and wars, and the Transitional Program treats imperialist militarism as a tool of capital.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from the defence of national self-determination and colonial struggles in the Transitional Program.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Trotsky's account of the revolution's religious policy favoured subordinating the church to civil power, though modern adherents mostly argue for separation.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: Trotskyists want officials to be recallable delegates, not an office above class and party.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from support for self-determination; Trotskyists accept it in principle, though revolution may override it.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred: autonomy arrangements are accepted in a workers' state but a capitalist region keeping its system is not a Trotskyist aim.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Trotsky rejected religion and any divine authority for rulers; the family chapter treats religious reaction as part of the bureaucratic Thermidor.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The program calls for expropriating capital and steeply taxing wealth, and a flat rate would favour the rich.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist materialism holds that social conditions shape people, and Trotsky argued the new society would remake the family and morality.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Trotsky condemned the bureaucracy's privileges and demanded officials be elected and recallable, with no one above the soviets.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from the stress on developing the productive forces; space is not discussed.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Soviet democracy rests on rule by the working majority, so a mixed constitution with aristocratic elements is rejected.

leader-cult.rationale: Trotsky attacked the cult of Stalin as a symptom of bureaucratic degeneration.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred from Trotsky's support for equality of women and the socialization of childcare; custody law is not addressed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Trotsky held that a privileged bureaucracy could rule a workers' state and even restore capitalism, so the struggle between classes and interests continues after the revolution.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Transitional Program calls for expropriating big landlords and giving land to the peasants who work it, under committees of farmers.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from support for the oppressed in colonial and national struggles; Trotsky did not address a refugee right of return as such.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Proletarian internationalism rejects nationalist territorial claims; inferred from internationalism applied to border claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Trotsky wrote against religious coercion and for freeing society from clerical power; inferred that punishing apostasy would be rejected.

women-must-cover.rationale: Trotsky condemned the subordination of women and the revival of traditional family norms; inferred that compulsory dress codes would be opposed.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred: the program backs a socialist United States of Europe but a shared currency under capitalist institutions is seen as a bloc of capital, not a goal.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred: internationalism favours class unity across borders, not unions built on shared ancestry or language.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: Marxists in this tradition favour self-determination and full equal rights over separate cultural-institutional autonomy; Trotsky's Jewish writings stress solving minority oppression through socialist revolution.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Trotsky argued Jews should fight anti-Semitism within the countries where they live through socialist revolution, and called a Zionist homeland a tragic mirage.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is the Marxist core, and Trotsky derived morality from class interests rather than from ideas.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred: the program answers monopolies by expropriation under workers' control, not by restoring competition.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred: the program opposes rescuing capitalists with public money, demanding expropriation of failing banks and firms instead.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: the tradition attacks bourgeois courts as class instruments, yet defends minority and workers' rights against majorities; adherents split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from Trotsky's support for women's emancipation; quotas are a modern, unaddressed tool.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Trotsky rejected autarky and socialism in one country, arguing the world division of labour is a force for socialism.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred: adherents back labour rights but see trade agreements as imperialist instruments, so they split.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred: Trotsky favoured material incentives and a stable currency during the transition, sliding wage scales included.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Trotskyism holds that revolution comes from mass working-class self-emancipation through soviets, and opposes substitutionist guerrilla action.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Abolishing privileged castes is a Marxist and Trotskyist aim; Trotsky condemned the bureaucracy's privileges.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from internationalism; Trotskyists treat a national narrative as secondary to class and world history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Trotskyism opposes imperialism and supports colonial liberation, as in the Transitional Program.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Transitional Program rejects national chauvinism and calls for workers' internationalism over patriotic loyalty.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from support for the struggles of oppressed groups; Trotskyists back anti-discrimination measures, though they stress class demands over preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from the Transitional Program's call to nationalise the banks into a single state bank, which would control credit.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Trotsky held that capitalism's contradictions bring it to its death agony, as the opening of the Transitional Program says.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Trotskyism opposes great-power domination and defends the oppressed nations of the former empires.

delink-world-market.rationale: Trotskyism rejects socialism in one country and delinking; it holds that backward countries can only advance through world revolution.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Trotskyism holds that workers of all countries share one class interest, and does not accept the labour-aristocracy thesis as a ground to write off workers.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Trotskyists treat discrimination as a tool of division and oppose it; the Transitional Program backs workers' defence against racial persecution.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Trotskyists defend civil liberties but treat bourgeois constitutions as class instruments, and favour soviets over entrenched legal guarantees.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from the Transitional Program's support for colonial peoples' self-determination.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Commune model Trotskyists endorse has elected, recallable officials and no hereditary rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism binds the minority to majority decisions once taken.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Trotskyists support mass resistance to oppressive rulers, though they do not rest it on constitutional law; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Commune is praised as a working body replacing parliamentarism; soviets, not parliament, hold power.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no settled Trotskyist position.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no settled Trotskyist position.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Their Morals and Ours rejects the morality of the ruling classes and treats ethics as class-based, so charity of the privileged is not a remedy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Transitional Program rests on mass working-class participation in struggle.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from Trotsky's view that ruling-class morality and ideology serve its order.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from the Transitional Program's view that reformist leaderships and democratic illusions tie workers to capital.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The Transitional Program describes imperialism as holding backward countries in subjection and draining them.

native-born-offices.rationale: Proletarian internationalism rejects reserving offices by birth or nationality.

party-own-road.rationale: Trotskyists opposed Moscow's dictation of national parties but also insist on centralized international organization.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The Revolution Betrayed rejects socialism in one country and autarky; development needs world revolution and the world division of labor.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from the class-based, internationalist outlook, which does not give priority to border claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the program is class-based rather than based on descent from pre-colonial peoples.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from the Transitional Program's call for workers' defense against fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Trotsky held the USSR a degenerated workers' state to be defended, and fascism a capitalist reaction; he did not treat them as equivalent.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: Marxists treat slavery as the core of the Civil War; the sources do not address it.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from class-based morality that sees honors to oppressors as serving the ruling class.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; Thermidor in the Family concerns women's emancipation, not male disadvantage.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on women's oppression in the family.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Permanent revolution and internationalism hold that socialism is not bounded by civilization.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Revolution Betrayed treats a military or bureaucratic caste ruling above the soviets as Bonapartism to be overthrown.

paid-care-work.rationale: Thermidor in the Family calls for socializing domestic labor; paying for it as labour is inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; Trotsky criticised the bureaucracy's revival of family authority, but adult duties to parents were not discussed.

office-by-exam.rationale: Trotsky favoured soviet election and workers' control of administration over examined officials; inferred, but he valued expertise.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Trotskyists favour nationalised key industries and a state monopoly of foreign trade, so blocking foreign takeovers fits; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Thermidor in the Family criticises the Stalinist restriction of divorce and defends easy dissolution of marriage.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Paris Commune model, which Trotsky endorsed, made delegates subject to instruction and recall at any time.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Transitional demands call for expanded public provision and expropriation, which opposes private pension accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The programme calls for expropriating large landowners and handing land to peasants' committees, which supports common control; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Soviet democracy as Trotsky described it needs elected councils to hold power over spending, though bourgeois parliaments are not his model.

single-official-language.rationale: Trotsky backed national cultural and language rights for minorities against Stalinist Russification; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: A planned economy would nationalise land, but Trotsky's writings do not address foreign land ownership; adherents split.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Trotskyists oppose racial oppression and would treat unequal outcomes as a sign of discrimination, but the classic sources do not address the legal test; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Marxists see consumer culture as a product of capitalism, but Trotsky wanted abundance for all; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Trotskyists oppose imperialist proxy wars, though they back revolutionary struggles against reaction; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Trotsky condemned Stalinist interventions to suppress workers' revolutions and national self-determination, as in the Soviet bureaucracy's conduct.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred: Trotsky held that big capital dominates bourgeois states, a view carried by later Trotskyists who call for open books and expropriation.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: Trotskyists are internationalist and oppose state sovereignty as an aim, so would not back national-sovereignty controls, though they oppose imperialist funding of opposition.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: Thermidor in the Family criticises state coercion of the family and Trotskyists treat births as a matter of free choice.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: Trotskyists oppose property privilege by locality and favour planned, equal access to housing across the working class.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Transitional Program calls for a sliding scale of hours and public works so that every worker has a job.

democratic-peace.rationale: Trotskyism holds that imperialist democracies wage war and that peace comes only through workers' revolution, not by spreading bourgeois democracy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Not addressed; Trotsky treated morality as class-historical in Their Morals and Ours, so obedience depends on the class interest served.

non-intervention.rationale: Trotskyists defend workers' states against imperialist intervention but support international revolutionary solidarity, so they reject absolute non-intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: The Transitional Program urges industrial unions and factory committees spanning whole workplaces and industries.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: On the Jewish Problem rejects the idea of Jewish conspiracy and holds antisemitism to be a reactionary tool of the ruling class.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Thermidor in the Family describes the early Soviet aim of the family's withering away and criticises the later restoration of legal marriage, but modern Trotskyists do not make abolishing legal marriage a demand.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Revolution Betrayed attacks bureaucratic secrecy and calls for open soviet democracy and transparency of the state.

local-production.rationale: Inferred: Trotskyists favour planned economy tied to world division of labour and reject autarky and socialism in one country.

informal-organisation.rationale: Trotskyism is a Leninist current built on a disciplined revolutionary party and democratic centralism.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Trotskyism is internationalist and holds that workers' power must override national law and borders.

religious-nation.rationale: Marxist internationalism rejects defining the nation by religion; Trotsky opposed religious nationalism.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: the Transitional Program backs the struggle of oppressed nations against imperialism, so ritual submission to a leading power is rejected.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: internationalism and a planned economy mean resources are pooled by need, not retained by region.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Marxist doctrine as the Transitional Program applies it expropriates the means of production while leaving personal belongings alone.

defeat-communism.rationale: Trotskyists are communists who defend the Soviet Union against imperialism despite its bureaucracy; they reject a drive to defeat communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The Transitional Program demands expropriation of key sectors under workers' control, not private providers inside a public system.

religion-illusion.rationale: Trotsky treats religion as a product of backwardness and oppression that fades as social conditions improve.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxists count capitalism as having developed the productive forces on which socialism builds; the program holds it is now in decay.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Revolution Betrayed argues that real equality for women needs the old family replaced through social and economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Trotsky laments the failure to replace the family with public kitchens, laundries and nurseries.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: proletarian internationalism opposes nationalist language purism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from Trotskyist support for national self-determination and minority rights, which implies honouring agreements with oppressed nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The program calls for centralised democratic planning on a national and international scale, not small self-governing communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: Trotskyism supports self-determination of national minorities and opposes chauvinist colonisation.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Trotskyists call themselves communists and hold that a workers' state, not a third way, replaces capitalism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: Trotsky held that the Jewish question could not be solved by a territorial claim in Palestine under imperialism, and ranked class over historic or religious claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Trotsky wrote against antisemitism and warned of the extermination of the Jews; Trotskyists treat the Holocaust as fascist barbarism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: Trotsky condemned the Stalinist reversal of the early revolution's family and sexual liberalism; modern Trotskyists oppose criminalisation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Trotsky called for soviet democracy with multiple working-class parties, but accepted suppressing counter-revolution and fascists.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: a materialist and secular tradition, which opposes persecution for religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Transitional Program demands independence for colonial and semi-colonial countries and opposes imperialist exploitation.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: anti-imperialist resistance is supported but as class struggle, not as a religious duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: Trotskyists oppose religious law and theocracy, favouring workers' power.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Trotsky held that soviets, workers' councils, are the form of mass self-rule and demanded workers' control of industry.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Trotskyists support struggle against racism and women's oppression as part of the class struggle, though many reject intersectionality as such; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred: modern Trotskyist groups support trans rights as part of liberation; Trotsky did not address it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from a humanist materialism; the sources do not discuss it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Trotskyism analyses politics by class and rejects blending left and right ideas.

alienated-labor.rationale: Alienation of labour is part of the Marxist critique Trotskyism builds on.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: the tradition is secular and internationalist and treats such claims as ideology that divides workers.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Their Morals and Ours rejects morality derived from divine commands and grounds ethics in class struggle.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Trotskyist groups differ on whether to oppose dress bans or defend secular state institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred: the Transitional Program champions workers against employers, which supports open complaints.

social-market-economy.rationale: The Transitional Program demands expropriation and a democratically planned economy.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Trotsky backed the Red Army and workers' militias, so abolition of armed forces is not Trotskyist, but it sees the state as withering away.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: the programme demands equality and a sliding scale of wages.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: Trotskyism defends the USSR against imperialism and opposes imperialist blocs, so it does not take neutrality as such.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Trotskyism rejects hereditary privilege, and Trotsky condemned bureaucratic privilege; hereditary office is inferred as rejected.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The Transitional Program calls for expropriating private banks into a single state bank, which differs from user-owned banks but agrees on ending profit-making credit; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The Transitional Program opposes imperialist domination of weaker countries and favours repudiating debts to it.

property-franchise.rationale: Soviet democracy is meant to extend political power to the working majority, not restrict it by wealth.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Trotsky backed women's liberation in the family, but linking it to nature is a modern eco-Marxist idea; inferred.

reification.rationale: Commodity fetishism is a Marxist core idea that Trotskyism inherits, though Trotsky rarely uses the term.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Marxist doctrine treats bourgeois liberties as formal while capital owns the means of expression; workers' control of the press follows.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Trotsky criticised bureaucratic arbitrariness and wanted soviet legality, but denied absolute legal limits on revolution; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Trotskyism stands for proletarian internationalism and equal rights across races and colonial peoples.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; broad participation fits soviet democracy so adherents likely welcome it; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: The Transitional Program demands abolition of business secrecy and open books, and Trotsky criticised bureaucratic secrecy.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Trotsky opposed religion's hold on family and law and favoured free personal life.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Trotsky fought anti-Semitism as reaction that divides the working class.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Trotsky grounded democracy in elected, recallable soviets of workers rather than lot-chosen citizens; sortition is not addressed, so inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Marxists regard religion as ideology to be superseded rather than reformed, and the sources do not address reinterpreting religious law; inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Transitional Program demands expropriating the capitalist magnates and holds that concentrated private wealth rules over workers' lives and the state.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed by Trotsky; inferred from the tradition's support for equal rights and opposition to oppression of minorities.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Trotsky backed scientific education and anti-religious propaganda but through persuasion, not compulsion; inferred from the chapter on religion and the family.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Trotskyists want police and army replaced by a workers' militia and armed people, not the end of all public safety institutions; inferred from that demand.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from the stress on class unity and soviet majority democracy over fixed communal shares.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The program rests on state-planned, workers-controlled provision rather than charity, which it treats as a poor substitute for guaranteed rights.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from the commune model of revocable, workman-wage officials, which curbs careers in office.

vote-delegation.rationale: Revocable delegates are a core soviet principle, though area-by-area delegation is a modern idea; inferred from that.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed in the 1930s texts; inferred from the tradition's concern about nuclear war and ecological crisis under capitalism.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Trotsky's chapter on the family demands full equality for women; extending that to religious office is an inference.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Thermidor in the Family criticises the compulsory family and the subordination of women and calls for real equality in the home.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from proletarian internationalism, which treats workers of all origins as one class, though it is not a specific Trotskyist demand.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the Transitional Program's demands for decent living conditions for all, which include housing.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred; an expropriated, democratically planned economy has no place for private monopolies on knowledge.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from working-class self-emancipation and opposition to nationalism, which rule out youth drilled for national service.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the Transitional Program's anti-militarist, anti-imperialist stance.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Opposition to imperialism is a core Trotskyist position, and foreign garrisons are seen as its instrument.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from Trotsky's writings on the Jewish question and his condemnation of national persecution.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Transitional Program calls for expropriating capitalist property and paying for work, not for ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Their Morals and Ours defends revolutionary violence and rejects absolute prohibitions on killing.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Trotskyism puts class and internationalism above nation, so it rejects continuous national essences.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred; Trotsky's analysis of the family treats gender roles as social products, but modern theory on sex is not covered.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; Trotskyists stress class unity while supporting women's liberation, so views split.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from Trotsky's materialist rejection of sacred nationalism.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Their Morals and Ours grounds politics in material class interests and rejects morality drawn from heaven.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Trotsky's writings on the Jewish question doubted that a territorial homeland would gather a people, but he did not address this question generally.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred; Trotskyism holds that seizing power and the economy create the conditions for a new culture.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; Trotskyists are materialist and indifferent to religious language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; Trotskyists reject religious authority yet do not adopt a test of religion by women's humanity.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Transitional Program demands equal rights and unity of workers across nationality and opposes national privilege.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and class politics, which do not seek regions defined by a single people.

independent-unions.rationale: Trotsky held that unions must be independent of the bureaucracy and run by their members, and the Transitional Program makes workers' control and union democracy central.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Trotsky called the USSR a degenerated workers' state, not socialism, because the bureaucracy had seized political power from the working class and needed a political revolution.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The Transitional Program calls for expropriating key industry and services under workers' control, which includes basic local utilities.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from Trotsky's preference for soviets as a single democratic workers' body; he saw no role for an upper chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: Trotskyism calls for nationally planned, expropriated industry under workers' democracy, not ownership by separate localities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Democratic centralism and a central plan mean joint bodies make binding decisions, unlike the confederal model.

family-wage.rationale: Transitional demands include a living minimum wage for workers' households, but Trotsky also opposed the bureaucracy's return to the traditional family; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by the Trotskyist sources; no basis for a position.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from Trotsky's optimism about science and planned technical progress under socialism.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the demand for a planned economy with state control of banking and credit.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; Trotskyists would favour privacy against the state but might see it as secondary.

person-over-state.rationale: Trotsky defended the dignity of the person against bureaucracy but rejected abstract morals above class interests, so the statement fits only partly.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Trotskyism is materialist and secular, so it does not hold that politics should serve a spiritual nature; inferred from its Marxist basis.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from democratic centralism, which keeps final authority with the central workers' body.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from Trotskyist faith in science and planned production for need; contested by ecosocialist strands.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from the classical Marxist aim of planned urban development and ending the town-country divide; weakly sourced.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Trotskyists prioritise class unity, though Trotsky backed self-organisation of oppressed groups such as Black workers; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from class internationalism; Trotsky also defended oppressed peoples' self-respect, so the answer is weak.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Trotskyism supports wars of oppressed peoples and revolutionary war against capitalism, and rejects defending its own bourgeois state; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Marxists treat nations as historical formations and put class above them; Trotsky held that national unity does not override class lines.

communal-electorates.rationale: Trotskyists reject dividing workers by religion and favour a single class-based soviet democracy.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Trotskyism treats nationalist claims of foreign plots as a way to hide class conflict, and locates the enemy in the ruling class at home.

free-public-college.rationale: The Transitional Program calls for free public services and education, and Trotskyists extend this to tuition-free universities.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Trotskyists favour planned expropriation of industry over market taxes and hold that polluters should be taken over; inferred, as the program predates the issue.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from socialist aims of planned production for human need; the sources do not address duties to future generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Trotskyists stress equality and class solidarity and reject essentialist claims about women; inferred from Trotsky on the family.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Transitional Program rejects bourgeois disarmament and calls for workers' militias and armed self-defence.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Trotsky as commissar for foreign affairs published the tsarist secret treaties in 1917, and the tradition opposes secret diplomacy; inferred from that record.

capital-controls.rationale: The Transitional Program demands a state monopoly of foreign trade and expropriation of banks, which implies full control over capital movements.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Transitional Program demands workers' militias and arming of workers, and the Commune model replaces the standing army with the armed people.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Trotskyists oppose imperialist wars and urge fraternisation across lines, but back revolutionary and defensive wars, so a blanket refusal is inferred only from anti-imperialist internationalism.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The program backs strong independent unions, factory committees and sliding scales of wages won through collective struggle, though it sees bargaining as only a step toward workers' control.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: the program demands a sliding scale of wages and hours and expropriation rather than state top-ups that subsidise low pay under capitalism.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from opposition to capitalist state limits on working-class demands; the program insists demands must not be bounded by what capitalism can afford.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Trotskyists reject reform of the imperialist order and seek its overthrow by revolution, so they agree with the aim of favouring the colonial world but not with 'restructuring the rules'.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Trotskyism follows Marx and Lenin that the bourgeois state must be overthrown and replaced by soviets, as in the Paris Commune.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Trotskyism holds to a democratically planned economy under soviet control rather than open-ended local experiments, though it values democratic debate about the plan.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: Marxists treat pricing nature as capital as extending commodification, and the program calls for expropriation rather than market valuation of resources.

sacred-nation.rationale: Proletarian internationalism rejects nationalism, treating the nation as a class-divided formation rather than a sacred community.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the demand for free public education and relief of the working class from debt; the program calls for cancelling peasant debts and similar burdens.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Trotskyists apply imperialism and uneven development mainly between states, and treat regional oppression case by case, so adherents are not clearly settled.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Trotsky's Their Morals and Ours rejects eternal moral truths and sees morality as class-conditioned, so a fixed human nature grounding rights is doubted.

public-service-media.rationale: Trotskyists want media under workers' control and distrust both state and commercial control, so funded 'independent' public media is not clearly endorsed or rejected.

missingStatements.text: Socialism cannot be built lastingly in one country alone; it requires revolution in other countries too.
missingStatements.rationale: Permanent revolution and opposition to socialism in one country are defining Trotskyist positions.

notes: Trotskyist groups differ on the nature of the USSR and other states (degenerated workers' state, state capitalism, bureaucratic collectivism) and on tactics such as entryism. Some answers on social issues rest on modern practice, not Trotsky's texts.
